option_a: a) Is more effective than expounding the principles then engaging the students in learning
option_b: b) Takes less time than the exposition learning approach
option_c: c) Helps students attain higher-level (life-skill) or methodological objectives as opposed to being passive receivers
option_d: d) Is best applied when students need to grasp a few basic concepts
rationale: Discovery (inquiry) learning engages learners actively in finding out for themselves, which is best suited to attaining higher-order/methodological and life-skill objectives rather than producing passive recipients. It typically takes MORE time and is not ideal for transmitting a few simple facts. (Ref: Nursing Education / principles of teaching & learning.)

stem: Q9. Micro-evaluation:
option_a: a) Enables the teacher to launch into new lines of argument when the students seem unconvinced
option_b: b) Enables students to benefit in some future learning situations
option_c: c) Should be minimal and limited if students are working together
rationale: Micro-evaluation is the moment-to-moment, formative feedback a teacher obtains DURING a lesson (e.g. reading the learners' reactions), allowing immediate adjustment of the teaching - such as opening new lines of explanation when students appear unconvinced. (Ref: Nursing Education / evaluation in teaching.)

stem: Q1. A leader who is mainly concerned with the day-to-day operations of an organisation with little regard to the future is called a:
rationale: A transactional leader focuses on day-to-day operations, supervision, exchange (rewards/penalties) and maintaining the status quo, rather than on vision and future transformation (the focus of a transformational leader). (Ref: Nursing Leadership & Management.)

stem: Q2. Zero-based budgeting means:
option_a: a) Multiplying current year expenses by a certain figure
option_b: b) Budgeting for purchase of major equipment
option_c: c) Use of a decision-making package to justify the current budget needs
option_d: d) Budget where accountability, efficiency and economy is emphasized
rationale: In zero-based budgeting every programme/activity starts from a 'zero base' and each manager must justify all requested funds afresh each period using decision packages - nothing is automatically carried over from the previous budget. (Ref: Nursing Leadership & Management - budgeting.)

stem: Q3. Mentors differ from preceptors in that mentors:
option_c: c) Have a short relationship with the novice staff
option_d: d) Do not assist the novice staff in career development
rationale: Mentoring is a voluntary, mutually chosen and usually long-term developmental relationship - the mentor chooses (and is chosen by) the protege and actively supports career development. A preceptor is normally assigned for a defined, shorter orientation period. (Ref: Nursing Leadership & Management / Education.)

stem: Q4. Over-delegation involves:
option_a: a) Delegating at the wrong time, to the wrong person, for the wrong reasons
option_b: b) Delegating to exceptionally competent employees
option_c: c) Transferring too many roles from the manager to the subordinates
rationale: Over-delegation is delegating TOO MUCH - transferring excessive tasks/roles (often including those the manager should retain) to subordinates, overloading them. (Improper delegation = wrong task/time/person; under-delegation = delegating too little.) (Ref: Nursing Leadership & Management - delegation.)

stem: Q38. A type of epilepsy in which psychological features are common is:
rationale: Temporal lobe epilepsy (complex partial seizures) is characteristically associated with psychological/psychic phenomena - auras, deja vu, fear, hallucinations of smell/taste, automatisms and mood/behavioural changes. (Ref: Psychiatric/Mental Health Nursing; Neurology.)

stem: Q7. It is difficult to obtain meaningful informed consent in qualitative research because the researcher does not know in advance how the study will evolve. This kind of consent gotten by qualitative research is called:
rationale: In qualitative research, because the design unfolds, consent is treated as an ongoing process - 'process consent' - in which the researcher repeatedly renegotiates the participant's continued agreement as the study evolves. (Ref: Nursing Research - qualitative methods/ethics.)

stem: Q8. Random assignment means:
option_a: a) Probability sampling where each subject has an equal and independent chance of participating in the study
option_b: b) Assigning subjects to the control and experimental group without predetermined criteria
option_c: c) Assigning subjects to the control group and experimental group such that each has an equal chance of being selected for each group
option_d: d) Random sampling method of assigning subjects to control group and experimental group
rationale: Random assignment (randomisation) is the allocation of subjects to study groups so that each participant has an equal and independent chance of being placed in EITHER the control or the experimental group - it controls for confounding. (Random selection/sampling, by contrast, concerns who gets INTO the study.) (Ref: Nursing Research - experimental design.)

stem: Q9. Practising nurses need to develop research-critique skills to:
option_a: a) Challenge fellow nurses doing research-report presentations
option_b: b) Be able to do literature review when doing their research studies
option_c: c) Participate fully in journal clubs
option_d: d) Judge the utility of research findings
rationale: The purpose of developing research-critique (appraisal) skills is to enable nurses to judge the quality and utility of research findings so they can decide whether and how to apply the evidence in practice (evidence-based practice). (Ref: Nursing Research.)

stem: Q10. Reflective scepticism, a characteristic of critical thinkers, means:
option_a: a) Asking awkward questions to challenge assumptions
option_b: b) Ability to imagine and explore alternatives
option_c: c) Taking a critical view of established dogmas and practices, scrutinizing them and questioning their current validity
option_d: d) Reflecting on past events and questioning them
rationale: Reflective scepticism is the disposition not to accept established dogmas/practices at face value - critically scrutinising them and questioning their current validity and evidence base. (Ref: Nursing Education - critical thinking.)

stem: Q11. Problem-based learning means:
option_a: a) Learning that results from the process of working towards the resolution of a problem
option_b: b) A situation where students learn without any assistance from the teacher
option_c: c) Learning that results after the learner gets the solution
option_d: d) Learning where teachers use questions only
rationale: Problem-based learning (PBL) is a student-centred approach in which learning arises from the PROCESS of working to understand and resolve a real or simulated problem; the teacher facilitates rather than abandons the learners. (Ref: Nursing Education - teaching/learning methods.)

stem: Q12. When an assessment tool measures what it is supposed to measure, it is said to have:
rationale: Validity is the degree to which an instrument actually measures what it is intended to measure. Reliability/consistency refers to the stability/reproducibility of the measurement. (Ref: Nursing Research / Educational measurement.)

stem: Q13. An appropriate method that can be used to teach the acquisition of psychomotor skills is:
rationale: Psychomotor (practical) skills are best taught by demonstration (and return demonstration), which shows the learner exactly how to perform the procedure step by step. Case studies and brainstorming target cognitive/affective domains. (Ref: Nursing Education - teaching methods.)

stem: Q14. The decision-making hierarchy is called:
rationale: The scalar chain is the formal line of authority and communication running from the top to the bottom of an organisation (the chain of command/hierarchy) along which decisions and instructions flow. Span of control is the number of subordinates a manager supervises. (Ref: Nursing Leadership & Management - organisation.)

stem: Q1. The following are clinical types of poliomyelitis: (i) Flaccid poliomyelitis  (ii) Abortive poliomyelitis  (iii) Non-abortive poliomyelitis  (iv) Non-paralytic poliomyelitis
rationale: The recognised clinical forms of poliomyelitis are abortive (ii), non-paralytic (iv) and paralytic - the latter being flaccid (i). 'Non-abortive' (iii) is not a recognised type and is the distractor, so the correct combination is i, ii, iv. (Ref: Park's/Kenyan Community Health & communicable disease texts; MOH Kenya EPI.)

stem: Q2. The following are examples of “spacing methods” of family planning:
option_a: a) Natural methods, chemical barriers, vasectomy
option_b: b) Mechanical barriers, tubectomy, chemical barriers
option_d: d) Chemical barriers, natural methods, mechanical barriers
rationale: Spacing (temporary/reversible) methods allow a couple to delay or space births; they include natural/fertility-awareness methods, chemical barriers (spermicides) and mechanical barriers (condoms, diaphragm). Vasectomy and tubectomy are PERMANENT (terminal) methods, so any option containing them is wrong. (Ref: MOH Kenya National Family Planning Guidelines.)

stem: Q4. A child with marasmus will present with the following clinical symptoms:
option_a: a) Oedema of the legs but not the face
rationale: Marasmus is severe wasting from energy deficiency: there is NO oedema, NO hepatomegaly, and NO skin/hair depigmentation - the child is markedly wasted ('old man face') and is usually alert with a relatively good appetite. Oedema, poor appetite, hair/skin depigmentation and a fatty enlarged liver are features of KWASHIORKOR. Hence 'no hepatic enlargement' is correct for marasmus. (Ref: Kenya IMNCI; MOH Kenya/WHO management of acute malnutrition.)

stem: Q5. In focused antenatal care:
option_a: a) The mother is encouraged to visit the antenatal clinic at least seven times during pregnancy
option_b: b) The mother is encouraged to save some money for buying baby clothes when born
option_c: c) The mother is encouraged to decide on the place of birth when labour begins
option_d: d) The mother is encouraged to make transport arrangements several months before her time of delivery
rationale: Focused (goal-directed) antenatal care emphasises birth preparedness and complication readiness - including arranging transport, finances, a skilled birth attendant and place of delivery well in advance. The classic FANC schedule was 4 goal-oriented visits (not seven), and the place of birth is planned during pregnancy, not when labour begins. (Ref: MOH Kenya Focused Antenatal Care guidelines / WHO.)

stem: Q6. In determination of disease incidence:
option_a: a) The total population is considered
option_b: b) The ability of disease to recur is not considered
option_c: c) Persons-years time at risk is considered
option_d: d) All the individuals suffering from the disease are considered
rationale: Incidence measures NEW cases arising over time; the incidence rate uses person-time (person-years) at risk as the denominator, counting only those at risk and the time each is observed. Prevalence (not incidence) counts all existing cases. (Ref: Epidemiology - Kenyan Community Health Nursing curriculum.)

stem: Q7. The demographic trends in Kenya indicate that since 1969 to date:
option_a: a) The crude birth rate has increased
option_b: b) The infant mortality rate has increased
option_c: c) Life expectancy at birth has increased
option_d: d) Total fertility rate has increased
rationale: Over the decades since 1969, Kenya's life expectancy at birth has risen, while the crude birth rate, infant mortality rate and total fertility rate have all declined (demographic transition). (Ref: KNBS / Kenya Demographic and Health Survey trends.)

stem: Q8. The following should be highly considered when counselling on family planning for an HIV-positive client:
option_a: a) Drug interactions between hormonal methods and anti-tuberculosis drugs
option_b: b) The client's current stage of AIDS
option_d: d) The client's economic status and source of funding
rationale: Many HIV-positive clients are on rifampicin-based TB treatment; rifampicin is a potent hepatic enzyme inducer that lowers the blood levels and effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives, so this drug interaction must be considered and an effective/back-up method advised. (Ref: MOH Kenya FP Guidelines; WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria.)

stem: Q9. When preparing a family for their parents' changed role due to HIV status, an important aspect to consider is:
option_d: d) Exercise schedule for the infected
rationale: Helping the family understand and accept the diagnosis - reducing stigma and discrimination (de-stigmatisation) toward the infected member - is the priority psychosocial preparation, as stigma undermines disclosure, support, adherence and the family's ability to adapt to changed roles. (Ref: MOH Kenya / NASCOP HIV psychosocial care guidelines.)

stem: Q10. The resolution stage of the grief response:
option_a: a) Lasts less than six months
option_b: b) May be prolonged if there has been a love-hate association
option_c: c) May be prolonged by anticipatory grieving
option_d: d) May be of less intensity if the affected has experienced a number of recent losses
rationale: Resolution of grief is prolonged when the relationship with the deceased was ambivalent (a 'love-hate' association) because of unresolved guilt and conflicting feelings. Anticipatory grieving generally EASES later grief, multiple recent losses tend to INTENSIFY grief, and there is no fixed time limit of under six months. (Ref: Mental Health/Psychiatric Nursing texts.)

stem: Q11. Mrs. Mama has laid down strict and rigid rules for her baby during toilet training. The characteristics the baby is likely to exhibit in adulthood include: (i) Stubbornness  (ii) Malevolence  (iii) Disorganisation  (iv) Stinginess  (v) Miserliness
rationale: According to Freud's psychosexual theory, conflict/over-strictness during the anal stage (toilet training) produces the 'anal-retentive' personality - obstinacy/stubbornness, orderliness, stinginess and miserliness. Hence i, iv and v. Malevolence and disorganisation are not features (disorganisation is the opposite of the anal-retentive trait). (Ref: Psychiatric/Mental Health Nursing; growth & development.)

stem: Q12. A patient tells a nurse “I felt very bad when my relatives visited me and I refused to talk to them”. The nurse's best response would be:
option_a: a) “Did they make you feel that way?”
option_c: c) “Do you think they came to visit you just to annoy you?”
option_d: d) “Describe what you were feeling just before your relatives visited you”
rationale: An open-ended, exploratory statement that invites the patient to describe their feelings ('Describe what you were feeling...') is the therapeutic communication technique of exploring/seeking clarification. The other options are closed, leading or challenging and block communication. (Ref: Therapeutic communication - Mental Health Nursing.)

stem: Q15. Benzhexol (Artane):
option_a: a) Should not be administered to patients with parkinsonian syndrome
option_b: b) May be used safely in patients with prostatic hypertrophy
option_c: c) Should never exceed 15 mg daily dosage
option_d: d) Does not cause orthostatic hypotension
rationale: Benzhexol (trihexyphenidyl, Artane) is an anticholinergic used to treat parkinsonism and drug-induced extrapyramidal effects; the usual maximum dose is about 15 mg/day. Being anticholinergic it is CONTRAINDICATED in prostatic hypertrophy (risk of urinary retention) - so (A) and (B) are wrong, and it can contribute to orthostatic hypotension. (Ref: Pharmacology texts; BNF.)

stem: Q16. Exhibitionism:
option_a: a) Occurs for less than 6 months
option_b: b) Occurs equally in both men and women
option_c: c) Is intensified when the perpetrator has excess free time and is under significant stress
option_d: d) Is more frequent in men without satisfying sexual relationships
rationale: Exhibitionism is a paraphilic disorder (recurrent urges/behaviour of at least 6 months' duration) seen predominantly in men; the urge to expose intensifies when the person has excessive free time or is under significant stress. Many exhibitionists do have satisfying adult sexual relationships, so (D) is incorrect. (Ref: Psychiatric/Mental Health Nursing; DSM criteria.)

stem: Q17. Children of divorced parents:
option_a: a) Experience distress and dysfunction more in the year preceding divorce
option_b: b) Experience less severe distress after two years of divorce as compared with those children remaining in conflictual marriages
option_c: c) Distress and dysfunction are lowest in the year after divorce
option_d: d) Have similar psychological problems with those of non-divorced parents
rationale: Research shows that, after about two years, children of divorced parents generally adjust and show LESS distress than children who remain in homes with ongoing high parental conflict - i.e., chronic marital conflict is more damaging than the divorce itself once adjustment occurs. (Ref: Child & Family Mental Health.)

stem: Q18. Mr. Moto has been constantly physically abusing his wife. Mr. Moto:
option_a: a) Is likely to have a diagnosable mental disorder
option_b: b) May predispose his anger on his children
option_c: c) May have come from a background in which violence is frequent and tolerated
option_d: d) May predispose himself to homicide
rationale: A learned/socialised history of violence - growing up in a family or environment where violence was frequent and tolerated - is the best-supported correlate of becoming a perpetrator of intimate-partner violence. Most abusers do NOT have a diagnosable mental disorder. (Ref: Mental Health Nursing - family/gender-based violence.)

stem: Q1. Community participation in primary health care (PHC) means the:
option_a: a) Community must build their health facilities
option_b: b) Community assumes responsibility for its health services
option_c: c) Leaders of the community should participate in health care
option_d: d) Members of the community should engage in health visits
rationale: A core principle of PHC (Alma-Ata) is community participation - the community is actively involved in planning, implementing and taking responsibility/ownership for its own health and health services, not merely receiving them. (Ref: Community Health Nursing - PHC principles; MOH Kenya.)

stem: Q2. In descriptive epidemiology the important characteristics of study are:
rationale: Descriptive epidemiology characterises the occurrence of disease by PERSON, PLACE and TIME - i.e. demographic data (age, sex, occupation, place, period). Prevalence, incidence and mortality rates are measures of frequency used within (and to support) analytic epidemiology. (Ref: Epidemiology - Kenyan Community Health curriculum.)

stem: Q4. To effectively combat endemic malaria, health workers should:
option_a: a) Distribute insecticide-treated mosquito nets and intensify health education
option_b: b) Spray larvicides and cut grass
option_c: c) Give more chemoprophylaxis and treat all cases
option_d: d) Provide mosquito nets and clear vegetation
rationale: Sustainable malaria control combines effective, proven vector control - long-lasting insecticide-treated nets (LLINs) - with health education to ensure correct, consistent use and prompt treatment-seeking. This integrated, community-based approach is more effective and sustainable than vegetation clearing or blanket chemoprophylaxis. (Ref: MOH Kenya National Malaria Control Programme guidelines.)

stem: Q6. The activities the nurse engages in during the preparatory phase of a home visit include:
option_b: b) Clarifying the source of the referral
rationale: The preparatory (pre-visit) phase is done before leaving for the home: the nurse reviews the records and CLARIFIES the source and reason for the referral, gathers relevant information and plans the visit. Locating the house occurs during the visit, and recording/reporting occurs after it. (Ref: Community Health Nursing - the home visit process.)

stem: Q24. The safe noise exposure level that does not cause damage to the tympanic membrane is:
rationale: The recommended safe occupational noise exposure limit is about 85 decibels (over an 8-hour day); prolonged exposure above this risks noise-induced hearing damage. (Ref: Occupational Health - Community Health Nursing.)

stem: Q25. The major practice roles of the occupational health nurse include:
rationale: The core practice roles of the occupational health nurse are as clinician (direct care/first aid/health surveillance) and administrator/manager of the occupational health service, in addition to educator, consultant and researcher roles. (Ref: Occupational Health Nursing.)

stem: Q28. The measures that would appropriately improve the health of the elderly include:
option_a: a) Mental health services, STI services
option_c: c) Home safety programmes, home-based services
rationale: Health promotion for the elderly focuses on safety and supporting independence - home safety programmes (preventing falls/injury) and home-based care services are the most appropriate measures for this age group. (Ref: Gerontological / Community Health Nursing.)

stem: Q29. Prevalence rate is defined as the number of:
option_a: a) Old and new cases of a specified disease existing at a given time
option_b: b) New cases of a disease in a population over a period of time
option_c: c) Old cases of a specified disease existing at a given time
option_d: d) Deaths from a specified disease or condition at a given time
rationale: Prevalence is the total number of existing cases (both old and new) of a disease present in a defined population at a given point (or period) in time. New cases over time describe incidence; deaths describe mortality. (Ref: Epidemiology - Community Health Nursing.)

stem: Q30. Some of the developmental tasks of a beginning family are:
option_a: a) Family planning, stabilizing the family unit
option_b: b) Family planning, relating to kin network
option_c: c) Relating to kin network, maintaining a stable marriage
option_d: d) Stabilizing the family unit, socializing children
rationale: In Duvall's family life-cycle, Stage I (the beginning/married-couple family) tasks include establishing a mutually satisfying marriage, RELATING to the kin network, and FAMILY PLANNING (deciding about children). Socialising children belongs to later stages. (Ref: Family Health / Community Health Nursing - Duvall's developmental tasks.)

stem: Q31. Some of the indirect client services provided by the community health nurse include:
option_a: a) Supervising the care provided, teaching
option_b: b) Teaching, health planning with consumers
option_d: d) Record keeping, supervising the care provided
rationale: Indirect care services are those performed on behalf of clients but not in direct face-to-face care - such as record keeping/documentation and supervising the care provided by others. Teaching, planning with consumers and bedside care are DIRECT services. (Ref: Community Health Nursing - roles of the CHN.)

stem: Q32. The components of the biological environment include:
rationale: The biological environment comprises living things and the products of living things that surround and sustain humans - including food sources and water supplies (which also harbour micro-organisms, plants and animals). Toxic substances, geographical features and natural resources are elements of the PHYSICAL environment. (Ref: Community Health Nursing - the environment and health.)

stem: Q33. The major service system of the community that is usually the focus of the citizen and the leadership of the community is:
rationale: The economic system (production, employment, income and resources) is the service system that most preoccupies community members and their leaders, because livelihoods and the community's capacity to support all other systems (including health) depend on it. (Ref: Community Health Nursing - community as a system/sub-systems.)

stem: Q34. The demographic parameters the community health nurse will examine while conducting a community diagnosis include:
rationale: Demographic parameters describe the population - its size, distribution/composition and vital statistics such as morbidity and mortality. Genetics and transport services are not demographic parameters. (Ref: Community Health Nursing - community diagnosis.)

stem: Q35. Vector-borne diseases include:
rationale: Vector-borne diseases are transmitted by arthropod vectors - plague by fleas and leishmaniasis by sand-flies. Dysentery is faeco-oral (water/food-borne) and rubella is spread by respiratory droplets, so neither is vector-borne. (Ref: Communicable disease / Epidemiology - Community Health Nursing.)

stem: Q36. A type of schizophrenia characterised mainly by delusions of persecution and auditory hallucinations is:
rationale: Paranoid schizophrenia is dominated by delusions (especially of persecution and/or grandeur) and auditory hallucinations, with relative preservation of cognition and affect. Disorganized type shows disorganized speech/behaviour and flat affect; catatonic shows marked psychomotor disturbance. (Ref: Psychiatric/Mental Health Nursing.)

stem: Q37. Postpartum depression (early postnatal mood disturbance) typically appears on:
rationale: The early, transient postnatal mood disturbance ('postpartum/maternity blues') typically appears about the 3rd-4th day after delivery, coinciding with hormonal changes and the onset of lactation, and usually resolves spontaneously within a few days. (True postpartum depression has a later, more insidious onset over weeks.) (Ref: Myles Textbook for Midwives; Mental Health Nursing.)
